questions.q: What is a service connection in Azure Pipelines?
options: A raw username and password pasted directly into a YAML file
A stored, authenticated link from Azure DevOps to an external service, referenced by name
A type of variable group used only for secrets
A Kubernetes resource that pipelines deploy automatically
questions.explain: A service connection is created once in Project Settings and referenced by name in YAML — the real credential is stored encrypted, never written into the pipeline file.

questions.q: Why does Northbridge Retail use separate service connections for staging and production instead of one shared connection?
options: Azure DevOps technically requires one connection per stage
Separate connections run pipelines faster
To scope access tightly, so a connection with production rights isn't reachable by every pipeline in the project
Shared connections are not supported by the Docker@2 task
questions.explain: Narrowly scoping connections per environment limits blast radius — a staging-only connection can't be used to touch production, even by mistake.

questions.q: What is a variable group used for?
options: Storing a pipeline's YAML trigger configuration
A named, reusable set of variables managed in the Library and shared across pipelines
Defining which agent pool a job runs on
Replacing the need for service connections entirely
questions.explain: A variable group holds shared configuration like a registry name or cluster name in one place, reused across as many pipelines as reference it.

questions.q: What's the advantage of linking a variable group to Azure Key Vault instead of storing secrets directly in the group?
options: Key Vault-linked variables run faster in pipeline logs
It removes the need for any approval gates
Azure Pipelines never stores the secret value — it fetches the current value from Key Vault at run time, so rotating a secret needs no YAML change
It allows secrets to be printed in plain text in build logs
questions.explain: A Key Vault-linked variable group fetches secret values at run time rather than storing them, so rotating a secret in Key Vault automatically updates every pipeline using it.

questions.q: In `azureSubscription: "northbridgeRetailACR"` inside an AzureCLI@2 task, what does that string refer to?
options: The literal name of the Azure subscription ID
A hardcoded secret value
The name of a service connection configured in the project
A Kubernetes namespace
questions.explain: azureSubscription here is the name of a service connection, not a subscription ID or a secret — the pipeline looks it up by name to authenticate.
